about: Own-words reads from the daily research task (ADMIS, Rabobank, Czapp and the news feed). fund_score: -1 bearish to +1 bullish, a judgement on the fundamental news only.

corn.fundamental: Dec recovers to ~439 (+0.8%) with a softer dollar and firmer crude, but weekly export sales fell from recent highs, so the demand story is cooling while fund selling has paused rather than reversed.
events: Weekly corn export sales decline (Dow Jones)
Chicago grains regain ground as dollar and oil ease pressure (Reuters)
Brazil's corn ethanol boom is speeding feedlot beef growth (Reuters)

soybeans.fundamental: Jan faded midday gains to ~1,207 (-0.8%); China holding imported beans at ports and swelling domestic stocks keep doubts about extra US buying alive, while late harvest progress in a few states adds little news.
events: Soybeans fade early gains to midday losses (Barchart)
China holds soybean imports at ports (Bloomberg)
States still harvesting soybeans (Successful Farming)

meal.fundamental: Meal slips ~0.8% to ~331 with beans while oil holds up; heavy crush keeps meal supply ample.
events: Soy complex fades midday (Barchart)
Strong crush pace (Brownfield)

oil.fundamental: Soyoil firms ~0.9% to ~60.4 with crude; supply from the heavy crush is ample, so the energy link remains the main driver.
events: Crude up on Middle East risk (Dow Jones)
Soyoil fell below support Wednesday (Barchart)

wheat.fundamental: Short covering continued with Dec ~579 (+1.6%), holding above the 578 R1 break; export sales helped, but Black Sea truce hopes and better US winter-wheat moisture leave the supply backdrop heavy.
events: Wheat rallying back on Thursday (Barchart)
Wheat export sales 345k t for 26/27 (USDA via Dow Jones)
El Niño seen improving US winter wheat outlook (Brownfield)

kc.fundamental: HRW leads the complex again (Mar ~641, +2.9%) in what still looks like short covering from oversold levels; Plains moisture remains a positive for 2027 supply.
events: KC wheat leads gains (CBOT via Yahoo)
Wheat rallying back on Thursday (Barchart)

cotton.fundamental: Old-crop has bounced with Dec back to ~76 (+1.4%) and Mar near 80 despite a firm dollar, a technical recovery rather than new supply news. Dec deliveries and the high-grade share of certificated stock still cap the comfort for longs until Mar is the lead month.
events: Strong dollar weighed on cotton early (ADMIS)
Dec ~76.0, Mar ~79.8 by midday (ICE via TradingView)
Texas yield trimmed again in USDA's November report (RFD-TV)

hogs.fundamental: Hogs extend the bounce off contract lows (Feb ~58.1, +1.7%), helped by the Thailand pork-access deal; current supplies are still heavy, so it reads as a relief rally.
events: Lean hogs firm with cattle Thursday (Brownfield)
Thailand deal includes US ag purchases and pork access (Successful Farming)

cattle.fundamental: Cattle rallied (Feb ~227.3, +1.5%) ahead of Friday's Cattle on Feed, where another very low placements number would confirm the shrinking feeder supply. Packer capacity additions such as Tyson's Allied Beef deal add demand for scarce cattle.
events: Cattle higher Thursday (Brownfield, Barchart)
Record-low placements possible in USDA Cattle on Feed (AgroLatam)
Tyson boosts Texas beef capacity (Farm Progress)

feeders.fundamental: Feeders follow live cattle higher (Jan ~335.9, +1.5%); cheap corn supports feeding margins and a low placements figure on Friday would underline tight feeder supply.
events: Cattle complex rallies (Barchart)
USDA Cattle on Feed due Friday (AgroLatam)
CME to cut feeder daily limits in December (DTN)

class3.fundamental: Dec Class III steadies near 17.0 after the block-led drop; US dairy exports on track for another record year are a demand support, but cheese supply keeps spot prices heavy.
events: US dairy exports heading for another record year (Dairy Herd)
Cheese blocks led losses Wednesday (Brownfield)

class4.fundamental: Record-pace dairy exports support NDM and butter demand; the Class IV nowcast still sits above futures on firm powder.
events: US dairy exports heading for another record year (Dairy Herd)
Dairy prices lower Wednesday (Brownfield)

palm.fundamental: Jan rebounds ~0.8% to ~4,288 with firmer crude and soyoil; no new supply data, so it is following the vegoil complex.
events: Jan ~4,288 (+35) (Bursa via TradingView)
Crude and soyoil higher (TradingView)

natgas.fundamental: Dec slides to ~3.26 (-3.3%), extending below 3.342 support; storage ending the season above normal outweighs slower Gulf LNG flows that favour US cargoes.
events: Natgas Dec ~3.26 (NYMEX via Yahoo)
LNG exports through Hormuz slow after attacks (Bloomberg)
US storage above normal (EIA)

crude.fundamental: WTI holds ~83.9 (+0.8%) even as equities drop ~2% and the dollar firms; Hormuz tanker attacks and Marathon's North Dakota force majeure offset ample Gulf and Russian exports, so supply risk is cushioning the risk-off tone.
events: Hormuz tanker attacks offset Gulf export surge (OilPrice.com)
Marathon force majeure on North Dakota deliveries (Seeking Alpha)
S&P 500 -1.9%, VIX ~28 (Yahoo)

ulsd.fundamental: Diesel slips ~0.5% to ~3.95 while crude firms; stocks are well below normal and cracks wide, but more barrels arriving, including a Russian-diesel tanker that briefly signalled a US port, and Bapco's restart lean bearish.
events: Tanker carrying Russian diesel briefly signalled a US port (Dow Jones/Kpler)
Bapco refinery heading back to full capacity (Reuters)
Distillate stocks stay below normal (EIA)

rbob.fundamental: RBOB edges up with crude, but last week's large gasoline build and stocks above normal keep the seasonal-demand picture soft.
events: Gasoline stocks rose 5.2 mb, above the 5-year norm (EIA)
Crude rebounds on Hormuz attacks (OilPrice.com)
